notes: Continuation of the second Coates letter, pencil folio 48. It finishes the inverse-polynomial proof, adds a characteristic-zero observation, gives an inverse-isomorphism corollary and discusses left inverses and semisimplicity. The degree-offset glyph is repeated in both exponents and in its integer declaration; the repetitions do not distinguish δ, d and j securely, so all three remain in place as alternatives. The overtypes in→it and an→of retain the old letters. The inverse identities were checked with their actual maps: from scan 048, u:B→A, v:A→B and w=uv give w^−1u=v^−1u^−1u=v^−1. In the corollary, write A=H^i(X), B=H^(i+2δ)(X′). The page’s two duality identifications a:A→A∨ and b:B→B∨ give the stated transpose-based map in the explicit form u′=a^−1u∨b:B→A. For w=u′u, t=w^−1u′ satisfies tu=I_A and ut=I_B, using the two isomorphisms u and u′; this verifies the displayed inverse formula. Existence and algebraicity of the duality identifications are the page’s premises, not separately proved here. The author’s “Maybe with some extra care”, “should hold”, “there should exist” and “it seems we need moreover” are retained as his qualifications. The later semisimplicity assertion was not proved in this run.
